literal: Ordered Central Firm General Yi Wei to attack them.
idiomatic: He ordered the Central Firm General Yi Wei to suppress them.

literal: Summoned Left Chancellor, Prince of Wei Yi back to the capital; ordered Lueyang Duke Zun to replace him garrisoning Zhongshan.
idiomatic: Prince Yi of Wei was recalled to the capital, and Duke Zun of Lueyang was left to hold Zhongshan.

literal: Summer, fourth month, day renxu: advanced Zun's enfeoffment to Prince of Changshan, Prince of Nan'an Yuan Shun advanced enfeoffment to Prince of Piling, Pacifying the Barbarians General Liyang Duke Mu Chong made Grand Marshal, Pacifying the South Duke Zhangsun Song made Minister of Works.
idiomatic: On the renxu day of the fourth month of summer Zun was made prince of Changshan, Shun prince of Piling, Mu Chong grand marshal, and Zhangsun Song minister of works.

literal: The emperor sacrificed to Heaven at the western suburb; banners and pennants had additions.
idiomatic: He sacrificed to Heaven at the western suburb with banners raised in greater splendor.

literal: Guangping Administrator, Liaoxi Prince Yuan Yilie plotted rebellion; within the commandery granted death, pardoned his wife and children.
idiomatic: Yuan Yilie of Liaoxi, administrator of Guangping, plotted treason and was ordered to take his own life in the commandery; his wife and children were spared.

literal: Fucheng Tujue Dong Qiang, Xingcheng Lushui Hao Nu, Hedong Shu Xue Yu, Di chief Fu Xing, each led their tribes to submit within the borders.
idiomatic: Dong Qiang of Fucheng, Hao Nu of Xingcheng, Xue Yu of the Shu in Hedong, and the Di chief Fu Xing each brought their tribes in submission.

literal: Sixth month, day bingzi: ordered the relevant offices to discuss and fix the state name.
idiomatic: On the bingzi day of the sixth month he ordered the ministries to choose a dynastic name.

literal: The host of ministers said: "Formerly before Zhou and Qin, generations dwelt in the soil where they were born; having state and family, when they ruled all under Heaven they inherited it as title.
idiomatic: The ministers said, "Before Zhou and Qin, rulers took their title from the land where they were born. When they came to rule the world, they kept that name."

literal: From Han onward, marquisates were abolished and defenders appointed; at the time there was no succession by generations; those who rose with the mandate all did not rely on resources of a foot of soil.
idiomatic: Since Han, hereditary fiefs gave way to appointed governors, and men who seized the mandate did not owe their rise to ancestral estates alone.

literal: Now the state is inherited for ten thousand generations, founding the enterprise at Yun.
idiomatic: Our house is to endure for ten thousand generations, with its foundation in the land of Yun.

literal: Your subjects consider that if one takes the long view, one should use Dai as the title.
idiomatic: We therefore urge that, for the long term, the dynasty be called Dai."

literal: The edict said: "Formerly my remote ancestor overall governed Youdu, controlled distant states; though he trod the royal throne, he did not fix the Nine Provinces.
idiomatic: The emperor replied, "Long ago our remote ancestor ruled Youdu and held sway over distant realms. Though he bore the royal title, he had not yet united the Nine Provinces.

literal: Reaching my person, residing in the season of the hundredth generation, all under Heaven split apart, the various Hu lacked a lord.
idiomatic: In my own time, at the end of an age of division, the Chinese lands had no true lord.

literal: [10] Though customs differ, comforting them lies in virtue; therefore I personally lead the six armies, sweep pacify the central land, ferocious rebels are swept away, the distant and near all submit.
idiomatic: [10] Customs may differ, but they are won by virtue. I have therefore led the six armies myself, swept the central plains clean of rebels, and brought the far and near to submission.

literal: It is fitting to continue the former title, taking Wei as the name.
idiomatic: It is right to keep our former name and call the state Wei.

literal: Proclaim throughout all under Heaven, all may know my intent."
idiomatic: Let this be proclaimed to all under heaven."

literal: Autumn, seventh month: moved the capital to Pingcheng, first built palace halls, established ancestral temple, set up altars of soil and grain.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn he moved the capital to Pingcheng, began the palace, founded the ancestral temple, and set up the altars of soil and grain.

literal: Yuyang Wuhuan Kuluguan Tao again gathered parties as bandits.
idiomatic: Kuluguan Tao of the Yuyang Wuhuan rebelled again.

literal: Ordered Champion General Wang Jian to attack and pacify them.
idiomatic: Wang Jian was sent to crush him.

literal: Eighth month: ordered the relevant offices to correct the capital demesne, regulate suburban fields, straighten roads and measures, mark roads and distances, balance the five weights, compare the five measures, fix the five gradations.
idiomatic: In the eighth month he ordered the ministries to survey the capital domain, regulate the suburbs, standardize roads and measures, and fix weights, volumes, and units.

literal: Sent envoys to tour commanderies and kingdoms, memorialize and report unlawful defending officials; personally viewed and inspected dismissals and promotions.
idiomatic: Envoys were sent through the commanderies to report corrupt magistrates, and he personally reviewed their promotions and dismissals.

literal: Ninth month: Wuhuan Zhang Nang's son Chao gathered fugitives, assembled parties of more than three thousand households, held Nanpi in Bohai, styled himself Eastern Campaign Grand General, King of the Wuhuan, plundered various commanderies.
idiomatic: In the ninth month Zhang Chao, son of the Wuhuan Zhang Nang, gathered three thousand rebel households at Nanpi in Bohai, styled himself king of the Wuhuan and eastern campaign general, and raided the commanderies.

literal: Ordered General Yu Yue to attack them.
idiomatic: Yu Yue was ordered against him.

literal: Winter, tenth month: began the Astronomy Hall.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter work began on the Astronomy Hall.

literal: Eleventh month, day xinhai: ordered Secretariat Personnel Section Director Deng Yuan to oversee office regulations, establish noble ranks, fix pitch pipes, harmonize music.
idiomatic: On the xinhai day of the eleventh month he put Deng Yuan in charge of offices, ranks, pitch pipes, and music.

literal: Rituals Section Director Dong Mi compiled rites for suburban altars, altars of soil and grain, court audiences, and feast ceremonies.
idiomatic: Dong Mi of the rituals section drafted the rites of the suburban sacrifices, the altars, court audiences, and banquets.

literal: Three Excellencies Section Director Wang De fixed laws and orders, declared prohibitions.
idiomatic: Wang De of the three excellencies section codified laws and penalties.

literal: Grand Astrologer Chao Chong made the armillary sphere, examined heavenly signs.
idiomatic: Chao Chong the grand astrologer built an armillary sphere and studied the heavens.

literal: Personnel Director Cui Xuanbo overall trimmed and judged them.
idiomatic: Cui Xuanbo of the personnel directorate supervised them all.

literal: Intercalary month: Left Chancellor, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Prince of Wei Yi and the host of kings, dukes, ministers, and scholars came to the palace gate and submitted a memorial saying: "Your subjects have heard the pole star at center, then the constellations align their shadows.
idiomatic: In the intercalary month Prince Yi of Wei and the nobles and ministers came to court with a memorial: "When the pole stands at the center, the stars wheel in their courses.

literal: The Son of Heaven follows Heaven, then the host below look up to his measure.
idiomatic: When the Son of Heaven follows Heaven, all below look up to his measure.

literal: We bow before Your Majesty's virtue harmonizing the two standards, Way towering to the Three and Five, benevolent wind spread over the four seas, flourishing transformation filling the great region, favor reaching insects, grace soaking trailing reeds, what songs belong to, the eight directions return in heart, where military might reaches, like wind over grass, the myriad people gazing eagerly, all wish to bind their lives.
idiomatic: Your virtue matches heaven and earth, your Way rivals the sage kings of old, your grace reaches even the insects and the grass at the roadside, and the eight directions turn to you as the grasses bend before the wind. All the people long to place their lives in your hands.

literal: Yet you personally practice humility, withdraw and place yourself after others; imperial bearing not yet displayed, dragon robes not yet worn — this is not what above fulfills Heaven's intent, below matches the heart of those who joyfully push you forward.
idiomatic: Yet you still hold back, refusing the imperial regalia. This neither fulfills Heaven's intent nor the people's wish to raise you up.

literal: It is fitting to glorify the sacred enterprise, display models and statutes to ten thousand generations.
idiomatic: You should glorify the sacred enterprise and show the model to ten thousand generations.

literal: Your subjects respectfully risk death to report.
idiomatic: We beg you, at the risk of our lives, to accept."

literal: The emperor thrice declined and then permitted it.
idiomatic: The emperor declined three times, then consented.

literal: Twelfth month, day jichou: the emperor attended the Astronomy Hall; Grand Marshal and Minister of Works advanced the seal and cord; the hundred offices all called ten thousand years.
idiomatic: On the jichou day of the twelfth month he took his seat in the Astronomy Hall; the grand marshal and minister of works presented the seal and cord, and the court shouted ten thousand years.

literal: Great amnesty, changed the era name.
idiomatic: He proclaimed a general amnesty and a new reign title.

literal: Posthumously honored Emperor Cheng and below and empresses with temple names and posthumous titles.
idiomatic: He posthumously honored Emperor Cheng and his predecessors, and gave posthumous titles to the empresses.

literal: Music used the Huangshi dance.
idiomatic: The court adopted the Huangshi dance for state ceremonies.

literal: Ordered the hundred offices to discuss and fix the dynastic phase; Secretariat Cui Xuanbo and others memorialized following the Earth phase, dress color esteemed yellow, numbers used five, end-of-year sacrifice at chen, victims used white, five suburbs established qi, proclaimed and assisted the seasons, respectfully bestowed the people's seasons, practiced Xia's correct calendar.
idiomatic: He ordered the ministries to fix the dynastic element; Cui Xuanbo urged the earth phase, yellow vestments, the number five, white victims, and the Xia calendar.

literal: Relocated the defending officials, powerful families, and people of two thousand households from six provinces and twenty-two commanderies to the capital at Dai.
idiomatic: Two thousand leading families from six provinces and twenty-two commanderies were moved to the capital.

literal: That year, Lan Han killed Murong Bao and established himself; Bao's son Sheng killed Han and presumptuously established himself.
idiomatic: That year Lan Han murdered Murong Bao and seized the throne; Bao's son Sheng killed Lan Han and declared himself ruler.

literal: Murong De styled himself King of Yan.
idiomatic: Murong De declared himself King of Yan.

literal: Year 2, spring, first month, day jiazi: first sacrificed to the Supreme Lord at the southern suburb, with Founding Ancestor Divine Yuan Emperor as associate; descended the altar to view the burning, completed the rites and returned.
idiomatic: In the second year, on the jiazi day of the first month of spring, he first sacrificed to Heaven at the southern suburb with the Divine Yuan Emperor as associate, watched the burning of the offerings, and returned when the rite was done.

literal: On day yichou, partial amnesty within the capital.
idiomatic: On the yichou day he granted a partial amnesty in the capital.

literal: First established the law of three carriages.
idiomatic: He instituted the protocol of the three imperial carriages.

literal: On day gengwu, the imperial carriage northern tour, separately ordered the generals in great raids on the Gaoche; Grand General, Prince of Changshan Zun and three armies from the eastern route exited Changchuan, Pacifying the North General Gaoliang Prince Yue Zhen and seven armies from the western route exited Niuchuan, the emperor personally led the six armies from the central route from Bochan Water northwest.
idiomatic: On the gengwu day he toured the north and sent his generals against the Gaoche. Prince Zun of Changshan marched east from Changchuan, Prince Yue Zhen of Gaoliang west from Niuchuan, and the emperor led the central column northwest from Bochan Water.

literal: Second month, day dinghai on the new moon: all armies met together, defeated more than thirty Gaoche mixed tribes, obtained more than seventy thousand persons, more than three hundred thousand horses, more than 1.4 million cattle and sheep.
idiomatic: On the new moon of the second month, the dinghai day, the columns united and broke more than thirty Gaoche tribes, taking seventy thousand people, three hundred thousand horses, and 1.4 million head of cattle and sheep.

literal: Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Prince of Wei Yi commanded thirty thousand cavalry separately from the northwest crossing the desert more than a thousand li, defeated their scattered remnants of seven divisions, obtained more than twenty thousand persons, more than fifty thousand horses, more than two hundred thousand cattle and sheep, Gaoche more than two hundred thousand carts, together with clothing, curios, and various objects.
idiomatic: Prince Yi of Wei with thirty thousand horse crossed the desert northwest more than a thousand li, shattered seven remnant bands, and took twenty thousand people, fifty thousand horses, two hundred thousand cattle and sheep, two hundred thousand Gaoche wagons, and countless goods.

literal: Returned and halted at Niuchuan and Bo Mountain, both carved stone to record merit, distributed rewards to accompanying ministers each according to rank.
idiomatic: The armies halted at Niuchuan and Bo Mountain, carved stones to record their deeds, and rewarded the officers by rank.

literal: On day gengxu, Pacifying the Barbarians General Yu Yue defeated Zhang Chao at Bohai.
idiomatic: On the gengxu day Yu Yue defeated Zhang Chao in Bohai.

literal: Chao fled to Pingyuan, was killed by his partisans.
idiomatic: Chao fled to Pingyuan and was killed by his own followers.

literal: Using the captured Gaoche masses, raised a deer park; south leaning on the terrace shade, north reaching the Long Wall, east enclosing Baideng, attached to Western Mountain, circumference several tens of li, chiseled canals to lead Wuchuan water into the park, dredged into three channels, divided flow inside and outside the palace city.
idiomatic: With the Gaoche captives he built a deer park south of the terrace, north to the Long Wall, east to Baideng, and west to the western hills, several tens of li around, and dug canals from the Wuchuan to feed three channels through and around the palace.

literal: Also dug Wild Goose Pool.
idiomatic: He also dug the Wild Goose Pool.

literal: Third month, day jiwei: the imperial carriage returned from the northern campaign.
idiomatic: On the jiwei day of the third month the court returned from the northern campaign.

literal: On day jiazi, first ordered the Five Classics and collected books each to set a Erudite, increased National University students by three thousand.
idiomatic: On the jiazi day he appointed erudites for the Five Classics, enlarged the National University by three thousand students.

literal: That month, Di man Li Bian rebelled against Murong De, sought rescue from Ye traveling Secretariat Director He Ba; Ba with light cavalry went to respond, captured Huatai, collected De's palace women and treasury.
idiomatic: That month the Di leader Li Bian rebelled against Murong De and called on He Ba at Ye; Ba rode to Huatai, took the city, and seized De's palace women and treasury.

literal: Also defeated De's Guilin King garrison and clerks, generals, and soldiers more than a thousand.
idiomatic: He also defeated the garrison of De's Guilin king and more than a thousand officers and men.

literal: On day bingzi, sent Establishing Righteousness General Yu Zhen, Rapid-as-Horses Commandant Xi Jin to attack Kudi division chief Ye Yigan, Youlian division chief Dou Yuni at Taihun River, defeated them; Kudi Qinzhi's son Tayeigan led his tribe to submit within the borders.
idiomatic: On the bingzi day he sent Yu Zhen and Xi Jin against Ye Yigan of the Kudi and Dou Yuni of the Youlian at Taihun River; after defeating them, Tayeigan son of Kudi Qinzhi submitted with his tribe.

literal: Zhen and others advanced and defeated the Houmochen tribe, obtained horses, cattle, and sheep more than one hundred thousand head, pursued and extinguished scattered remnants, entered Da'e Valley.
idiomatic: Yu Zhen pressed on, broke the Houmochen, took more than a hundred thousand livestock, pursued the fugitives into Da'e Valley.

literal: Zhongshan Administrator Qiu Ru hid in Zhao commandery, pushed bandit Zhao Zhun as lord, styled Envoy Bearing Staff, Grand General Western Campaign, Governors of Ji and Qing, Duke of Julu, Qiu Ru as Zhun's chief clerk, gathered parties and fanned sedition.
idiomatic: Qiu Ru, administrator of Zhongshan, hid in Zhao, set up the bandit Zhao Zhun as leader with forged titles, and stirred rebellion.

literal: Ordered Central Guard General Zhangsun Fei to attack and pacify them.
idiomatic: Zhangsun Fei was sent to crush them.

literal: Summer, fourth month: former Qinghe Administrator Fu Shi gathered parties of more than a thousand households, styled himself Pacifying the Army General.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer the former Qinghe administrator Fu Shi raised more than a thousand households and styled himself pacifying army general.

literal: Fifth month, day guihai: Pacifying the Barbarians General Yu Yue attacked and defeated them.
idiomatic: On the guihai day of the fifth month Yu Yue defeated him.

literal: Autumn, seventh month: began the Tianhua Hall.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn work began on the Tianhua Hall.

literal: On day xinyou, great review at the deer park; feast rewards each according to rank.
idiomatic: On the xinyou day he held a great review in the deer park and feasted his officers.

literal: Chen commandery and Henan floating migrants more than ten thousand mouths inwardly relocated; sent envoys to inquire after and comfort them.
idiomatic: More than ten thousand refugees from Chen and Henan were resettled inland, and envoys were sent to comfort them.

literal: Yao Xing sent masses to besiege Luoyang; Sima Dezong's general Xin Gongjing requested rescue.
idiomatic: Yao Xing besieged Luoyang; Xin Gongjing of the Jin court begged for aid.

literal: Eighth month: sent Grand Marshal Mu Chong leading six thousand cavalry to go to their aid.
idiomatic: In the eighth month Mu Chong was sent with six thousand horse to relieve the city.

literal: Increased and opened the capital's twelve gates.
idiomatic: The twelve gates of the capital were enlarged and opened.

literal: Built the Western Armory.
idiomatic: The western armory was built.

literal: Remitted half the rent and levies of commandery and prefecture people.
idiomatic: Rent and levies were halved throughout the commanderies.

literal: On day xinhai, ordered ritual officers to prepare and compile the mass of ceremonies, set down in the new statutes.
idiomatic: On the xinhai day he ordered the ritual officers to codify the state ceremonies in the new statutes.

literal: Fanyang man Lu Pu gathered masses on the seacoast, styled Envoy Bearing Staff, Grand General Northern Campaign, Regional Inspector of Youzhou, attacked and plundered commanderies and counties, killed Regional Inspector of Youzhou Feng Tagan.
idiomatic: Lu Pu of Fanyang gathered a host on the coast, took forged titles as northern campaign general and inspector of Youzhou, raided the districts, and killed the inspector Feng Tagan.

literal: Murong Sheng's Liaoxi Administrator Li Lang raised the commandery to submit within the borders.
idiomatic: Li Lang, Murong Sheng's administrator of Liaoxi, brought his commandery in submission.

literal: Xihe Hu chief Hunuoyu, Dingling chief Zhai Tong, Shu chief Han Long, all together led their tribes to submit within the borders.
idiomatic: Hunuoyu of Xihe, Zhai Tong of the Dingling, and Han Long of the Shu each submitted with their tribes.

literal: Winter, tenth month: the Grand Temple completed; moved the Divine Yuan, Pingwen, Zhaocheng, and Xianming emperors' spirit tablets to the Grand Temple.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter the Grand Temple was completed and the tablets of the Divine Yuan, Pingwen, Zhaocheng, and Xianming emperors were installed.

literal: Twelfth month, day jiawu: Murong Sheng's Pacifying the Barbarians General, Administrator of Yan commandery Gao Hu, led three thousand households to submit within the borders.
idiomatic: On the jiawu day of the twelfth month Gao Hu, Sheng's general and administrator of Yan, submitted with three thousand households.

literal: On day xinhai, ordered Material Officers General He Tu to attack Lu Pu.
idiomatic: On the xinhai day He Tu was ordered against Lu Pu.

literal: The Tianhua Hall was completed.
idiomatic: The Tianhua Hall was completed.

literal: That year, Lü Guang established his son Shao as Heavenly King, styled himself Supreme Emperor.
idiomatic: That year Lü Guang made his son Shao heavenly king and took the title of supreme emperor himself.

literal: Guang died; bastard son Zuan killed Shao and presumptuously established himself.
idiomatic: When Guang died, his bastard son Zuan murdered Shao and seized the throne.

literal: [11] Tufa Wugu died; younger brother Lugu replaced him, sent envoys with court tribute.
idiomatic: [11] Tufa Wugu died; his brother Lugu succeeded him and sent envoys to court.

literal: Year 3, spring, first month, day wuwu: He Tu defeated Lu Pu at Liaoxi, captured alive Pu and his son Huan, sent in escort to the capital, executed by dismemberment.
idiomatic: In the third year, on the wuwu day of the first month of spring, He Tu defeated Lu Pu in Liaoxi, took him and his son Huan alive, and had them torn apart at the capital.

literal: On day guihai, performed the ceremony at the northern suburb.
idiomatic: On the guihai day he sacrificed at the northern suburb.

literal: Separately ordered the various offices to tour the provinces, observe the people's customs, inspect and memorialize the unlawful.
idiomatic: He sent officials through the provinces to observe customs and report misconduct.

literal: Bestowed cloth and silk on the host of ministers each according to rank.
idiomatic: He gave cloth and silk to his ministers according to rank.

literal: Second month, day dinghai: ordered the relevant offices to sacrifice to the sun at the eastern suburb.
idiomatic: On the dinghai day of the second month he ordered sacrifice to the sun at the eastern suburb.

literal: First plowed the sacred field.
idiomatic: He performed the first plowing of the sacred field.

literal: On day renyin, the imperial son Cong died.
idiomatic: On the renyin day the prince Cong died.

literal: Third month, day wuwu: established Empress Murong clan.
idiomatic: On the wuwu day of the third month he made Lady Murong empress.

literal: That month, dug the southern city canal communicating within the city, made eastern and western fish ponds.
idiomatic: That month he dug a canal from the south into the city and made fish ponds east and west.

literal: Summer, fourth month: Yao Xing sent envoys with court tribute.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer Yao Xing sent envoys to court.

literal: Fifth month, day wuchen: ordered Master of Guests Zhang Ji as envoy to Yao Xing.
idiomatic: On the wuchen day of the fifth month Zhang Ji was sent as envoy to Yao Xing.

literal: On day jisi, the imperial carriage eastern tour, then visited Zhuolu, sent envoys with great sacrifice to sacrifice at the temples of Emperor Yao and Emperor Shun.
idiomatic: On the jisi day he toured east to Zhuolu and sent envoys with great victims to sacrifice at the shrines of Yao and Shun.

literal: West to Mayi, viewed the Lei source.
idiomatic: He went west to Mayi to view the Lei springs.

literal: Autumn, seventh month, day renzi: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: On the renzi day of the seventh month of autumn he returned to the palace.

literal: Began the Central Heaven Hall and Mica Hall, Jinhua Chamber.
idiomatic: Work began on the Central Heaven Hall, the Mica Hall, and the Jinhua Chamber.

literal: Eleventh month: Gaoche separate commander Chilejian led more than nine hundred encampments to submit within the borders.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month Chilejian, a Gaoche sub-chief, submitted with more than nine hundred camps.
